headline: IVANHOE Q1: Kamoa-Kakula Copper C1 Costs Hit $2.58/lb, Kipushi Sets Record 65,044-Tonne Zinc Quarter
snippet: Ivanhoe Mines released Q1 2026 results on May 6 (investor call May 7), reporting adjusted EBITDA of $191M including $158M attributable from Kamoa-Kakula — where C1 copper costs came in at $2.58/lb, below the $2.60–$3.00 guidance range. Kipushi set a zinc production record at 65,044 tonnes, and Ivanhoe upsized its 2026 group exploration budget to $127M with $86M allocated to the Makoko District in the Western Forelands.

headline: BARRICK'S BIGGEST WEEK: AGM Friday, Q1 Earnings Monday, and a 40% Dividend Hike Up for Scrutiny
snippet: Barrick Mining (NYSE: B) faces its most consequential week of the year: the AGM on May 8 will test shareholder support for the company's new dividend policy targeting 50% of attributable free cash flow, with the base quarterly dividend raised 40% to $0.175/share. Q1 2026 results land May 11, with analysts forecasting $0.79 EPS on $4.76B revenue — the weakest quarter of the year as management flagged softer gold and copper production in Q1.

headline: EAGLE NUCLEAR KICKS OFF PERMITS at US's Largest Conventional Uranium Deposit — 32.75M lb U3O8, Oregon-Nevada Border
snippet: Eagle Nuclear Energy (NASDAQ: NUCL) has initiated pre-drill environmental baseline studies at its Aurora Uranium Project — the largest conventional measured-and-indicated uranium resource in the US at 32.75M lbs U3O8 near the Oregon-Nevada border. A 47-hole, 27,000-foot drill program launches in July 2026, targeting a pre-feasibility study in H2 2027 as the US works to cut its 95% dependence on imported uranium.

headline: OPUS ONE GOLD DRILLS 8.22 g/t Au Over 8.5m in Abitibi's Winter Campaign — Zone 1 Keeps Expanding
snippet: Opus One Gold Corp (TSX-V: OOR) reported winter 2026 drill results from its Noyell property in Quebec's Abitibi greenstone belt, with hole NO-26-07 returning 8.22 g/t Au over 8.5m (true width 7.16m) in the eastern sector of Zone 1. A second hole (NO-26-10a) returned 5.68 g/t Au over 1.3m in Zone 1's centre, building the case for a continuous high-grade corridor.

headline: ARIZONA EAGLE EXPANDS MCCABE: 5.73 g/t Au Over 4.2m Confirms Mineralization Extends Northeast of Historic Resource
snippet: Arizona Eagle Mining (TSX-V: AZEM) reported Phase 1 drilling at the historic McCabe gold-silver mine in Arizona intercepted a 4.2-metre sulfide-rich quartz vein grading 5.73 g/t Au and 5.90 g/t Ag — including 0.8m at 11.35 g/t Au — confirming that high-grade mineralization extends northeast beyond the historic resource footprint. The company says the intercept opens a new vector for the broader district.

headline: BONANZA SILVER RETURNS TO THE COBALT CAMP: Nord Precious Metals Pulls 2,343 g/t Ag (9,510 g/t Peak) at Castle East
snippet: Nord Precious Metals (TSX-V: NTH) reported hole CS-26-129W2 at Castle East in Ontario's historic Cobalt Camp intercepted 2,343 g/t Ag (68 oz/ton) over 1.85m, including a peak interval of 9,510 g/t Ag (277.6 oz/ton) over 0.30m alongside elevated cobalt, nickel, copper, and zinc. The company has launched a fully funded 5,000m next drill phase as part of its ongoing 30,000m program.

headline: PECOY COPPER ADDS THIRD DRILL RIG in Peru as 35,000m Program Targets Three Copper-Gold Zones Simultaneously
snippet: Pecoy Copper (TSX-V: PCU) mobilized a third drill rig at its eponymous copper-gold-molybdenum-silver project in southern Peru, simultaneously advancing the Center of the Pit, Central Breccia, and South Breccia zones. The move expands active drilling capacity within the company's 35,000m diamond drill program, testing high-priority copper porphyry targets in a proven South American district.

headline: BRAZIL'S GOLD RUSH HEATS UP: Explorers Gain Ground as $4,700 Gold Draws Capital Into the Tapajós and New Belts
snippet: Junior and mid-tier gold explorers are accelerating programs across Brazil's Tapajós, Gurupi, and emerging greenstone belts as record gold prices attract fresh capital to a jurisdiction that sat largely dormant during the 2022–2024 downcycle. Active programs surveyed include GoldMining's São Jorge two-rig, 8,000m drill in the Tapajós district, where early holes returned 12m at 2.38 g/t Au with a 22 g/t high-grade interval.

headline: CAN THE $2.8B SERRA VERDE DEAL CRACK CHINA'S RARE EARTH MONOPOLY? A Geopolitical Reality Check
snippet: The Diplomat examines whether USA Rare Earth's $2.8B acquisition of Serra Verde Group — including a 15-year offtake with guaranteed floor prices — can meaningfully challenge China's grip on NdPr and magnet metals supply. The analysis weighs Serra Verde's Brazilian clay-hosted ionic resource against China's entrenched processing dominance, and considers what a Brazilian court challenge to the deal could mean for the Western supply chain effort.
